# FDG9054

> DO implement dependency properties by calling instance methods `DependencyObject.GetValue` and `DependencyObject.SetValue`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.3.1 Dependency Property Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9054
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Implement the accessor of the dependency property '{0}' with {1}

FDG9054 reports, in the CLR property of a dependency property, which is a property P of a class derived from DependencyObject that declares a static DependencyProperty field named P followed by "Property", a get accessor that does not call DependencyObject.GetValue with the field, or a set accessor that does not call SetValue with the field (or with a DependencyPropertyKey field named P followed by "PropertyKey"). Wrappers whose field has another name or is declared in another class are not seen, so coverage is partial. FDG9057 reports accessors that make the call and do more; a SetValue call whose value is not the value parameter is FDG9057's. The fix rewrites the accessor body; there is no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
public class TextButton : DependencyObject {

   public string Text {
      get { return (string)GetValue(TextProperty); }
      set { SetValue(TextProperty, value); }
   }

   public static readonly DependencyProperty TextProperty = ...
}
```
